title: Finding
description: A research finding and the evidence that supports it. A finding is never written as the plain fact of one article: it carries document-level evidence and its own confidence.

statement.description: The finding, stated as a claim.

confidence.description: How well the evidence supports the statement, 0-1. This is a confidence in the claim, kept separate from any weight and never a factual accuracy rate.

importance.description: How much this finding matters to the research objective, 0-1.

evidence.description: The document-level evidence behind the finding. At least one item is required so a finding is always traceable.

document_id.description: The document this piece of evidence comes from.

evidence_type.description: Whether this document supports, contradicts or partially supports the statement.

quote.description: A short permitted excerpt; omitted when retention does not allow quoting.

locator.description: Where in the document the evidence sits, for example a section heading or paragraph index.

note.description: Why this document counts as evidence for or against the statement.

scope.description: The conditions under which the statement holds, so it is not over-generalised.

limitations.description: What the finding does not establish, and what could weaken it.

follow_up.description: The next question this finding raises.

weight.description: Ranking weight derived from the scoring dimensions, 0-1. Used for ordering only; it is not the confidence in the statement.
